generic: Recombinant Follicle Stimulating Hormone (Follitropin alfa / beta)
pharm: Fertility agent; follicle-stimulating hormone for ovulation induction and spermatogenesis
quick: Individualised; women often start 75-150 IU/day SC
summary: Recombinant FSH (follitropin alfa or beta) is a recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone produced in CHO cells. In women it stimulates ovarian follicular development for ovulation induction (e.g., in anovulatory PCOS) and for controlled ovarian stimulation in assisted reproductive technology (ART). In men it stimulates spermatogenesis in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (with hCG). It is given by subcutaneous injection under specialist supervision with careful follicular monitoring. It is NOT separately FDA-listed under this descriptor here; this record reflects EMA/SmPC (e.g., Gonal-f, Puregon) labelling.
indications: Anovulation (including PCOS) in women unresponsive to clomifene — ovulation induction
Controlled ovarian stimulation for multiple follicular development in assisted reproductive technologies (IVF/ICSI)
Stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (with concurrent hCG)

dosage.d: Start 75-150 IU daily; adjust by >=37.5 IU at intervals of >=7 days
dosage.t: Daily until adequate follicle, then hCG
dosage.n: Max usually 225 IU/day; individualise to response

dosage.d: Start 150-225 IU daily; adjust to ovarian response (max ~450 IU/day)
dosage.n: Give hCG 24-48 h after adequate follicular development

dosage.d: 150 IU three times weekly with hCG
dosage.t: For at least 4 months (often up to 18)
dosage.n: Pre-treat with hCG to normalise testosterone

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection (commonly abdomen/thigh), rotating sites
Reconstitute powder forms gently; do not shake; use pen devices per instructions
Use only under the supervision of a specialist in fertility/reproductive medicine
Coordinate timing of the ovulatory hCG trigger with follicular monitoring
Discard if the solution is cloudy or contains particles
moa: Recombinant FSH is biologically identical to endogenous follicle-stimulating hormone. In women it binds FSH receptors on ovarian granulosa cells, promoting growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and increasing estradiol production; an ovulatory dose of hCG (or LH) then triggers final maturation and ovulation. In men, FSH acts on Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis, which also requires adequate intratesticular testosterone provided by concurrent hCG.

absolute: Tumours of the hypothalamus or pituitary gland
Ovarian, uterine, or breast cancer (women); testicular/prostate cancer (men)
Ovarian enlargement or cysts not due to PCOS
Primary ovarian failure / primary testicular failure
Conditions incompatible with pregnancy (e.g., uncontrolled thyroid/adrenal disease, pituitary tumour)
relative: Risk factors for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (PCOS, high antral follicle count, young age, high estradiol)
History of tubal disease (ectopic pregnancy risk)
monitor: Ovarian response by transvaginal ultrasound and serum estradiol

preg: Recombinant FSH is not indicated during pregnancy and is stopped once ovulation/conception is achieved. There is no indication for use in established pregnancy.
renal: No specific dosing data; use only under specialist supervision.
hepatic: No specific dosing data; use only under specialist supervision.

moderate: Concomitant clomifene citrate may enhance the follicular response
Co-administered hCG/LH is part of standard protocols (triggers ovulation/supports spermatogenesis)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitoring is by transvaginal ultrasound (follicle number/size) and serum estradiol; FSH assays are not used to titrate during treatment.

serious: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) — may be severe with ascites, haemoconcentration, thromboembolism
emergency: Severe OHSS (rapid weight gain, severe abdominal pain, breathlessness, reduced urine output)

monitoring: Transvaginal ultrasound to track follicle number and size
Serum estradiol to assess response and OHSS risk
Signs and symptoms of OHSS (abdominal distension, weight gain, breathlessness)
Thromboembolic risk; pregnancy outcome (including ectopic and multiple pregnancy)
In men: semen analysis to assess spermatogenesis
counsel: Injections are given under specialist fertility supervision; learn correct self-injection technique and site rotation
Attend all scheduled ultrasound and blood-test appointments for monitoring
Report severe abdominal pain, bloating, rapid weight gain, breathlessness, or reduced urination immediately (possible OHSS)
Be aware of the increased chance of twins or higher-order multiple pregnancy
Store the medicine as directed (usually refrigerated; some pens may be kept at room temperature for a limited period)
Do not use if the solution is cloudy or past its expiry
pk: Follicular growth develops over days of daily dosing
Serum FSH peaks ~12-24 hours after subcutaneous dose
Steady state reached in 3-4 days with daily dosing
Refrigerate 2-8C; protect from light; some pens may be stored at room temperature per labelling
pearls: Recombinant follitropin (alfa/beta) is produced in CHO cells — purer and more consistent than urinary FSH; this record reflects EMA/SmPC labelling (e.g., Gonal-f, Puregon), not a standalone FDA entry
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is the key serious risk — monitor with ultrasound and estradiol and individualise dosing, especially in PCOS
An hCG (or LH) ovulatory trigger is given once follicles are mature; withhold if excessive response to reduce OHSS
Strongly associated with multiple pregnancy — counsel patients accordingly
Specialist-only use with structured follicular monitoring
In men, must be combined with hCG to provide intratesticular testosterone for spermatogenesis
missed: If a daily injection is missed, contact the fertility clinic for advice rather than doubling the dose — timing is critical to the stimulation protocol and monitoring schedule.
overdose: The effects of overdose are unknown but excessive stimulation could precipitate ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Management is supportive, focused on OHSS prevention/treatment (fluid management, thromboprophylaxis, drainage of ascites if needed) and withholding further FSH and the hCG trigger.
